stories.headline: The Thing in the Pocket Is a Stone: Ridge Flint, Unmarked, Warm to the Touch; Steve's Four Words Now Make Partial Sense
stories.byline: By our Hollow Correspondent, filing from the kitchen table
body: The item removed from a coat pocket upon return to the household yesterday morning and placed upon the kitchen table has been identified. It is a stone. Specifically: a piece of ridge flint, approximately the size of a wren's egg, dark grey with one face worn smooth by water that has not touched it in some time. It is not, sources confirm, magical in any registered sense. It is, sources also confirm, warm.

Steve's four margin words — written in the same economical hand responsible for 'Harlan's Hollow' three weeks prior — can now be partially decoded in light of this development. The first word is 'ridge.' The fourth word is 'keeps.' The middle two words remain under assessment. Christine, who memorised the access road in both directions before the wheels turned and can still recite it, has examined the stone and described it as 'the right shape for a pocket.' This has been accepted as a complete statement.

The duck, last observed facing due south at the second waymarker, has not been repositioned. The third mark on the chart — half a mile above the second circle, on the unnamed ridge where the stone was found — now has a small annotation beside it in Christine's hand. The annotation is a single word. It has not been shared with this correspondent, but the ridge has been named, which means the chart has changed, which means the hollow gave something back that the hollow did not have to give.

stories.headline: Duck Subcommittee Convenes; Learns of Southward Reorientation; Adjourns to Lie Down
body: The Ministry's newly formed Duck Orientation Subcommittee, established by emergency memo on Friday afternoon and staffed by three officials who had not previously considered ducks within their professional remit, convened at nine o'clock this morning to address the matter of the Jellico duck's southward reorientation at the second waymarker.

The subcommittee had prepared three theories, a flowchart, and a strongly worded request for the duck to present itself for formal registration. Upon being informed that the duck is rubber, is charmed by no known hand, arrived on a Jeep mirror without witnesses, and has since been moved back to its position on the mirror facing north-northeast by Steve, who described this as 'setting it right,' the subcommittee requested a ten-minute recess. The recess has now run forty minutes. The flowchart has not been recovered.

The Ministry confirmed in a brief statement that 'the duck situation remains under active non-understanding' and requested that any future reorientations be reported no sooner than they occur. A second memo, issued eleven minutes later, rescinded the first and requested that all reorientations be reported immediately. A third memo, issued four minutes after that, confirmed that both previous memos remain in effect simultaneously. This is not unusual.

stories.headline: Sunday Rest Observed; Bank Closed; Accounts Holding Steady; Griphook the Younger Reached by Owl Anyway and Advised Not to Be
body: Gringotts Wizarding Bank observed its weekly closure today, a fact that has been true every Sunday for four hundred years and continues, sources note, to surprise no one except Griphook the Younger, who sent an owl at half past eight regarding a discrepancy in the Thornwick portfolio that he characterised as urgent.

The owl was received. A reply was dispatched within the quarter hour. The discrepancy, upon examination, was not a discrepancy. Griphook the Younger has been advised that Sunday is not a business day, that the Thornwick portfolio has been in order since Thursday, and that the owl has been gently returned with a note attached indicating that future Sunday correspondence will be answered on Monday and that this policy is not a new one. The portfolio is fine. It was always fine. Christine knew it was fine on Thursday.

stories.headline: Stone Assessed by All Household Parties; Verdicts Filed; Table Population Grows by One
body: The ridge flint currently occupying the centre of the kitchen table was subjected to independent assessment by all three household familiars this morning, with results consistent with their established characters. Lucy circled the stone twice, sat at a precise distance of fourteen inches, and filed no report. Her expression suggested she had already determined its provenance, value, and any associated leverage, and had chosen not to share this information. Investigators note this is entirely in keeping with her known operating procedure.

Ellie approached the stone with great interest, sniffed it for a sustained period, then sniffed it again as though the first sniff had been performed by someone else. She has since returned to it twice. Jersey did not approach the stone directly but elected to fall asleep on the kitchen floor in its general vicinity, which this correspondent interprets as an endorsement. The table, which has held charts, ropes, trail guides, annotated road notes, and a hand-winch in recent weeks, appears to have accepted a stone as its new purpose without complaint.

familiars_corner: Lucy: The stone arrived in a coat pocket. Lucy knows which coat. Lucy knows the pocket. Lucy has decided this information is worth holding.
Ellie: The stone smells like outside, which is where outside is, and Ellie has now confirmed this four times and considers the matter still open.
Jersey: The kitchen floor near the table is warm, the stone is warm, and Jersey has arranged himself so as to be adjacent to both, which is the only geometry that matters.
founding_editor_note: That stone's got good weight — you keep something with good weight. I've got a level from 1987 that still reads true and I'd like to see anyone argue with it. — D.

in_brief.sport: Sunday rest observed across all competitive disciplines; the only weight moved today was the biscuit tin, origin of movement unconfirmed.
in_brief.forecast: Fog lifts from the ridge by ten; the stone stays warm regardless; the chart has a new name on it and the week ahead knows.

storyline_updates.title: What the Hollow Gave Back
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: The unexpected thing has been revealed — a piece of ridge flint, warm to the touch, found on the unnamed ridge above the second circle. Steve's four margin words are now partially decoded: 'ridge' is first, 'keeps' is fourth; the middle two remain unresolved. Christine has added a single-word annotation to the third chart mark — the ridge now has a name, but it has not been published. The duck has been restored to its north-northeast position by Steve. The Ministry's duck subcommittee has adjourned indefinitely. Day 4 — the final day — should resolve the arc with the revelation of Christine's annotation (the ridge's name), the meaning of Steve's two middle words, and a small moment of completion: the chart fully marked, the stone settled in its place, the hollow having given back what it had.
